rules.covers: Every endpoint in the admin API group calls the role check first
Any endpoint whose path starts with admin, including app/admin/stats
Every read and write of tenants filters on org_id

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Role list is exactly admin or support_lead
org_id filter value matches the caller's org (tenant isolation against request-supplied org_id)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists; compare_to would also block cross-org support staff, so it needs an owner decision

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Who holds which role and how roles are granted
Only admin endpoints are checked; a new admin endpoint outside api/admin with no /admin path is not seen
ask_parts_not_covered.why: other: scoping is by group and path

assumptions: '/admin' means the admin API group (canonical admin) plus any endpoint whose URL path starts with admin, so app/admin/stats is included
'filtering by org_id' means a where condition on org_id; the endpoints' request-supplied org_id is not checked against the caller
The role check should run before any db call, so it is the first statement; the precondition message is generic
Advisory enforcement is right for a new policy per the skill; the customer decides whether to make it blocking
confusions: The skill's AUTH-002 example uses tags or paths; for a whole API group the catalogue has api_groups, which the template text does not mention for this check. I used api_groups plus a second rule for paths.
Scope params are written as top-level params in the rule. Worked, but the skill's 'Fill' list does not say which scope params a template may take.

I wrote the precondition condition as a var with || in its value. I did not find a worked XanoScript example of an OR in a precondition in this workspace; I assumed the var form is valid. Dry-run accepted the function.
The dry run listed three creates but none of the five endpoint updates. I could not tell whether it omits updates or did not detect the edits. Not explained by the docs I had.
wished_for: A check or param that says a function's role list matches a given set (or that the role check compares the right field)
A worked example of a policy whose rules scope an API group and a path together, or the rule for OR-ing scopes
Dry-run output that lists updated endpoints, not only creates
dry_run_problems_seen: Function "require_role" not on this branch (parse warning; expected before push, cleared by the dry run's CREATE)
Dry run listed no UPDATE lines for the five modified endpoints
why_confidence: The role check is enforced as first statement on all admin endpoints, so the 'before doing anything else' part is covered by AUTH-002. The role set itself and the org_id value are not checked, so the goal is only partly met. Tenant rule only checks that a filter exists, not that it matches the caller.
